page.layout: One page of running text, no margin notes. Running head and page number at the top. Above the main text, a four-line mnemonic verse; then paragraphs of text; then a Barbara syllogism with side numbers at the right of its lines; no notes, catchword or signature.

main_text.l: Barbara,celarent,prima:darij,ferióque,
Cafare[?],camestres,festino,baroco, secunda:
Tertia grande sonans dedit,darapti,felapton.
Adiungens,disamis,datisi,bocardo,firizon.
Primæ autem figuræ hæc ratio est, vt Barba-
ra valeat ad rem ex toto confirmandam: Cela-
rent ad rem ex toto refellendam: Darij ad rem
ex parte cōfirmandam : Ferio ad rem ex parte
refellendam.
Age, quis est primus primæ figuræ modus?
Cùm è propositione & assumptione vtraque
& vniuersali,& affirmatiua,vniuersalis & affir-
matiua conclusio cogitur. atque hoc quidem
primo modo genus omne quæstionis tractari
potest: sed cautio adhibenda est, vt propositio
sit vniuersalis,& assumptio affirmatiua.
Bar Omne animal est mortale 2
ba Omnis homo est animal 1.4 3
ra Ergo omnis homo est mortalis. 3
Quodnam huius syllogismi firmamentum
est? Medium est ex genere ad speciem, cuius
hoc firmamentum est: Quod generis proprium
est, idem speciei quoque proprium est. Nam
propositio proprij affectione continetur. Pro-
prium enim animalium est mori. quod cùm de
inanimatis dicitur, veluti de stirpibus, trásla-
tè dicitur. assumptionem verò generis affectio
sustinet.
Quis est secundus? Cùm è propositione
vniuersali negatiua & assumptione vniuersali

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "Cafare" is marked [?]; the printed form may be Cesare, and the first line is copied as it looks on the scan. The side numbers 2, 1.4, 3 and 3 beside the syllogism are placed at the ends of its lines; their exact position beside the brace is unclear. The accent in "trásla-tè" and the mark over the o in "cōfirmandam" are read as printed. Long s is normalised to s throughout, so "est" and "potest" stand where the printer set "eft" and "poteft". "firizon" is copied as printed. Spelling is otherwise as printed, with u/v and i/j normalised.
